title: Ensure unprivileged eBPF is disabled
description: eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) allows programs to be loaded and executed within kernel context. Unprivileged users should not be able to load eBPF programs. On Azure Container Linux the kernel parameter kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled is set to 1.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4.8 Ensure unprivileged eBPF is disabled

audit.command: chk() { p=$1; allowed=" $2 "; case $p in net.ipv6.*) [ -d /proc/sys/net/ipv6 ] || return 0;; esac; v=$(sysctl -n "$p" 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$p: not available"; return 1; }; case "$allowed" in *" $v "*) ;; *) echo "$p is $v (running)"; return 1;; esac; sd=$(readlink -e /lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl || readlink -e /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-sysctl); f=$("$sd" --cat-config 2>/dev/null | grep -Po "^\h*${p//./\.}\h*=\h*\K\H+" | tail -n1); [ -n "$f" ] || { echo "$p is not set in any sysctl configuration file"; return 1; }; case "$allowed" in *" $f "*) ;; *) echo "$p is $f in configuration"; return 1;; esac; }; if chk kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled 1; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Set the following parameter in /etc/sysctl.conf or a file in /etc/sysctl.d/ ending in .conf: kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled = 1 Example: # printf '%s\n' "kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled = 1" >> /etc/sysctl.d/60- kernel_sysctl.conf Run the following command to set the active kernel parameter: # sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1

title: Ensure sshd GSSAPIAuthentication is disabled
description: The GSSAPIAuthentication parameter specifies whether user authentication based on GSSAPI is allowed.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.11 Ensure sshd GSSAPIAuthentication is disabled

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: sshd not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'sshd -T | grep gssapiauthentication' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'gssapiauthentication no' || { echo step1: missing 'gssapiauthentication no'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the GSSAPIAuthentication parameter to no above any Include and Match entries as follows: GSSAPIAuthentication no Note: First occurrence of an option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.

reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.12 Ensure sshd HostbasedAuthentication is disabled

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/ssh/sshd_config file to set the HostbasedAuthentication parameter to no above any Include and Match entries as follows: HostbasedAuthentication no Note: First occurrence of a option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.

title: Ensure sshd PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled
description: The PermitEmptyPasswords parameter specifies if the SSH server allows login to accounts with empty password strings.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.19 Ensure sshd PermitEmptyPasswords is disabled

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: sshd not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'sshd -T | grep permitemptypasswords' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'permitemptypasswords no' || { echo step1: missing 'permitemptypasswords no'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config and set the PermitEmptyPasswords parameter to no above any Include and Match entries as follows: PermitEmptyPasswords no Note: First occurrence of an option takes precedence, Match set statements withstanding. The SSH daemon must be restarted for the changes to take effect. To restart the SSH daemon, run the following command: # systemctl reload-or-restart sshd.service

title: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled
description: The PermitRootLogin parameter specifies if the root user can log in using SSH. The default is prohibit-password.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.20 Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: sshd not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'sshd -T | grep permitrootlogin' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'permitrootlogin no' || { echo step1: missing 'permitrootlogin no'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

If Include locations are enabled, used, and order of precedence is understood in your environment, the entry may be created in a file in Include location.

title: Ensure re-authentication for privilege escalation is not disabled globally
description: The operating system must be configured so that users must re-authenticate for privilege escalation. Audit: Passes when no uncommented !authenticate tag exists in /etc/sudoers or /etc/sudoers.d.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.1 Ensure re-authentication for privilege escalation is not disabled globally

audit.command: grep -rEq "^[^#]*!authenticate" /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null && echo noncompliant || echo compliant

remediation.command: Configure the operating system to require users to reauthenticate for privilege escalation. Based on the outcome of the audit procedure, use visudo -f <PATH TO FILE> to edit the relevant sudoers file. Remove any occurrences of !authenticate tags in the file(s).

title: Ensure sudo authentication timeout is configured correctly
description: sudo caches used credentials for a default of 5 minutes. This is for ease of use when there are multiple administrative tasks to perform. The timeout can be modified to suit local security policies. Audit: Passes when every timestamp_timeout in /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d is between 0 and 15 minutes; with none set the sudo default of 5 minutes applies.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.2 Ensure sudo authentication timeout is configured correctly

audit.command: bad=0; for v in $(grep -rhoP "timestamp_timeout=\K-?[0-9.]*" /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null); do case $v in -*|"") bad=1;; *) [ "${v%.*}" -le 15 ] 2>/dev/null || bad=1;; esac; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: If the currently configured timeout is larger than 15 minutes, edit the file listed in the audit section with visudo -f <PATH TO FILE> and modify the entry timestamp_timeout= to 15 minutes or less as per your site policy. The value is in minutes. This particular entry may appear on its own, or on the same line as env_reset. See the following two examples: Defaults env_reset, timestamp_timeout=15 Defaults timestamp_timeout=15 Defaults env_reset

title: Ensure password creation requirements are configured
description: The pam_pwquality.so module checks the strength of passwords. It performs checks such as making sure a password is not a dictionary word, it is a certain length, contains a mix of characters (e.g. alphabet, numeric, other) and more. The following are definitions of the pam_pwquality.so options. The following options are set in the /etc/security/pwquality.conf file: Password Length: • minlen = 14 - password must be 14 characters or more Password complexity: • minclass = 4 - The minimum number of required classes of characters for the new password (digits, uppercase, lowercase, others) -OR- • dcredit = -1 - provide at least one digit • ucredit = -1 - provide at least one uppercase character • ... Audit: Passes when /etc/security/pwquality.conf sets minlen to 14 or more, sets minclass=4 or all four dcredit/ucredit/lcredit/ocredit to negative values, and pam_pwquality has retry=1..3 in /etc/pam.d/system-password and /etc/pam.d/system-auth.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.1 Ensure password creation requirements are configured

audit.command: q=/etc/security/pwquality.conf; [ -r $q ] || exit 1; bad=0; v=$(awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*minlen[[:space:]]*=/{gsub(/[[:space:]]/,"",$2);print $2}' $q | tail -1); [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 14 ] || bad=1; c=$(awk -F= '/^[[:space:]]*minclass[[:space:]]*=/{gsub(/[[:space:]]/,"",$2);print $2}' $q | tail -1); if [ "${c:-0}" -ne 4 ]; then for k in dcredit ucredit lcredit ocredit; do x=$(awk -F= -v k=$k '$1 ~ "^[[:space:]]*"k"[[:space:]]*$"{gsub(/[[:space:]]/,"",$2);print $2}' $q | tail -1); [ -n "$x" ] && [ "$x" -lt 0 ] || bad=1; done; fi; for p in /etc/pam.d/system-password /etc/pam.d/system-auth; do grep -Pq "^\h*password\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?pam_pwquality\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?retry=[1-3]\b" $p 2>/dev/null || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Edit the file /etc/security/pwquality.conf and add or modify the following line for password length to conform to site policy: minlen = 14 Edit the file /etc/security/pwquality.conf and add or modify the following line for password complexity to conform to site policy: minclass = 4 -OR- dcredit = -1 ucredit = -1 ocredit = -1 lcredit = -1 Edit the /etc/pam.d/system-password and /etc/pam.d/system-auth files to include the appropriate options for pam_pwquality.so and to conform to site policy: password requisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3

title: Ensure lockout for failed password attempts is configured
description: Lock out users after n unsuccessful consecutive login attempts. • deny=<n> - Number of attempts before the account is locked • unlock_time=<n> - Time in seconds before the account is unlocked Note: The maximum configurable value for unlock_time is 604800. Audit: Passes when every pam_faillock auth line in /etc/pam.d/system-password and /etc/pam.d/system-auth has deny between 1 and 5 and unlock_time 0 or at least 900, and each file has such lines.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.2 Ensure lockout for failed password attempts is configured

audit.command:
bad=0; for p in /etc/pam.d/system-password /etc/pam.d/system-auth; do l=$(grep -P "^\h*auth\h+[^#
]+\h+pam_faillock\.so\s+" $p 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$l" ] || { bad=1; continue; }; for d in $(printf "%s
" "$l" | grep -oP "deny=\K[0-9]+"); do [ "$d" -ge 1 ] && [ "$d" -le 5 ] || bad=1; done; for u in $(printf "%s
" "$l" | grep -oP "unlock_time=\K[0-9]+"); do [ "$u" -eq 0 ] || [ "$u" -ge 900 ] || bad=1; done; printf "%s
" "$l" | grep -q "deny=" || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Set password lockouts and unlock times to conform to site policy. deny should be not greater than 5 and unlock_time should be 0 (never), or 900 seconds or greater. Edit the files /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/system-password and add the following lines: Modify the deny= and unlock_time= parameters to conform to local site policy, Not to be greater than deny=5: Add the following lines to the auth section: auth required pam_faillock.so preauth silent audit deny=5 unlock_time=900 auth [default=die] pam_faillock.so authfail audit deny=5 unlock_time=900 The auth sections should look similar to the following example: Note: The ordering on the lines in the auth section is important. The preauth line needs to below the line auth required pam_env.so and above all password validation lines. ...

title: Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512
description: The commands below change password encryption from md5 to sha512 (a much stronger hashing algorithm). All existing accounts will need to perform a password change to upgrade the stored hashes to the new algorithm. Note: • These changes only apply to accounts configured on the local system. • Additional module options may be set, recommendation only covers those listed here. Audit: Passes when pam_unix.so on the password stack of /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/system-password uses the sha512 option.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.3 Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512

audit.command: bad=0; for p in /etc/pam.d/system-auth /etc/pam.d/system-password; do grep -Pq "^\h*password\h+([^#\n\r]+)?\h+pam_unix\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?sha512\b" $p 2>/dev/null || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Edit the /etc/pam.d/system-password and /etc/pam.d/system-auth files to include sha512 option and remove the md5 option for pam_unix.so: password sufficient pam_unix.so sha512 Note: • Any system accounts that need to be expired should be carefully done separately by the system administrator to prevent any potential problems. • If it is determined that the password algorithm being used is not SHA-512, once it is changed, it is recommended that all user ID's be immediately expired and forced to change their passwords on next login, In accordance with local site policies.

title: Ensure password reuse is limited
description: The /etc/security/opasswd file stores the users' old passwords and can be checked to ensure that users are not recycling recent passwords. Audit: Passes when pam_pwhistory.so on the password stack of /etc/pam.d/system-password and /etc/pam.d/system-auth sets remember to 5 or more.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.4.4 Ensure password reuse is limited

audit.command: bad=0; for p in /etc/pam.d/system-password /etc/pam.d/system-auth; do grep -Pq "^\h*password\h+[^#\n\r]+\h+pam_pwhistory\.so\h+([^#\n\r]+\h+)?remember=([5-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\b" $p 2>/dev/null || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: Edit both the /etc/pam.d/system-password and /etc/pam.d/system-auth files to include the remember option and conform to site policy as shown: Note: Add or modify the line containing the pam_pwhistory.so after the first occurrence of password requisite: password requisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=5 Example: (Second line is modified) password requisite pam_pwquality.so try_first_pass local_users_only authtok_type= password requisite pam_pwhistory.so use_authtok remember=5 retry=3 password sufficient pam_unix.so sha512 shadow try_first_pass use_authtok password required pam_deny.so

title: Ensure password expiration is 365 days or less
description: The PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to force passwords to expire once they reach a defined age. It is recommended that the PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter be set to less than or equal to 365 days. Audit: Passes when PASS_MAX_DAYS in /etc/login.defs and the maximum age of every account with a password in /etc/shadow are between 1 and 365 days.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5.1.1 Ensure password expiration is 365 days or less

audit.command: bad=0; [ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1; v=$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*PASS_MAX_DAYS[[:space:]]/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs | tail -1); [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 1 ] && [ "$v" -le 365 ] || bad=1; for x in $(awk -F: '$2 ~ /^[^*!xX]/ && $2 != "" {print ($5==""?"99999":$5)}' /etc/shadow); do [ "$x" -ge 1 ] && [ "$x" -le 365 ] || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Set the PASS_MAX_DAYS parameter to conform to site policy in /etc/login.defs: PASS_MAX_DAYS 365 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --maxdays 365 <user>

title: Ensure minimum days between password changes is configured
description: The PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to prevent users from changing their password until a minimum number of days have passed since the last time the user changed their password. It is recommended that PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter be set to 1 or more days. Audit: Passes when PASS_MIN_DAYS in /etc/login.defs and the minimum age of every account with a password in /etc/shadow are 1 day or more.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5.1.2 Ensure minimum days between password changes is configured

audit.command: bad=0; [ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1; v=$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*PASS_MIN_DAYS[[:space:]]/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs | tail -1); [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 1 ] || bad=1; for x in $(awk -F: '$2 ~ /^[^*!xX]/ && $2 != "" {print $4}' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null); do [ "$x" -ge 1 ] 2>/dev/null || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Set the PASS_MIN_DAYS parameter to 1 in /etc/login.defs: PASS_MIN_DAYS 1 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --mindays 1 <user>

title: Ensure password expiration warning days is 7 or more
description: The PASS_WARN_AGE parameter in /etc/login.defs allows an administrator to notify users that their password will expire in a defined number of days. It is recommended that the PASS_WARN_AGE parameter be set to 7 or more days. Audit: Passes when PASS_WARN_AGE in /etc/login.defs and the warning period of every account with a password in /etc/shadow are 7 days or more.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5.1.3 Ensure password expiration warning days is 7 or more

audit.command: bad=0; [ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1; v=$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*PASS_WARN_AGE[[:space:]]/{print $2}' /etc/login.defs | tail -1); [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 7 ] || bad=1; for x in $(awk -F: '$2 ~ /^[^*!xX]/ && $2 != "" {print $6}' /etc/shadow 2>/dev/null); do [ "$x" -ge 7 ] 2>/dev/null || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Set the PASS_WARN_AGE parameter to 7 in /etc/login.defs: PASS_WARN_AGE 7 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --warndays 7 <user>

title: Ensure inactive password lock is 30 days or less
description: User accounts that have been inactive for over a given period of time can be automatically disabled. It is recommended that accounts that are inactive for 30 days after password expiration be disabled. Audit: Passes when the INACTIVE default in /etc/default/useradd (as shown by useradd -D) and the inactivity period of every account with a password in /etc/shadow are between 0 and 30 days (-1 or an empty field means no lock and fails).
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5.1.4 Ensure inactive password lock is 30 days or less

audit.command: bad=0; [ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1; v=$(sed -n "s/^INACTIVE=//p" /etc/default/user[a]dd 2>/dev/null | tail -1); [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" -ge 0 ] && [ "$v" -le 30 ] || bad=1; for x in $(awk -F: '$2 ~ /^[^*!xX]/ && $2 != "" {print ($7==""?"-1":$7)}' /etc/shadow); do [ "$x" -ge 0 ] && [ "$x" -le 30 ] || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set the default password inactivity period to 30 days: # useradd -D -f 30 Modify user parameters for all users with a password set to match: # chage --inactive 30 <user>

title: Ensure all users last password change date is in the past
description: All users should have a password change date in the past. Audit: Passes when no account with a password in /etc/shadow has a last-change date later than today.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5.1.5 Ensure all users last password change date is in the past

audit.command: [ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1; t=$(( $(date +%s) / 86400 )); awk -F: -v t=$t '$2 ~ /^[^*!xX]/ && $3 != "" && $3+0 > t {f=1} END{exit f}' /etc/shadow && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Investigate any users with a password change date in the future and correct them. Locking the account, expiring the password, or resetting the password manually may be appropriate.

title: Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0
description: The usermod command can be used to specify which group the root account belongs to. This affects permissions of files that are created by the root account.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.5.3 Ensure default group for the root account is GID 0

audit.command: alt0() { command -v cut >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: cut not installed"; return 1; }; command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'grep "^root:" /etc/passwd | cut -f4 -d:' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 0 || { echo step1: missing 0; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set the root account default group to GID 0 : # usermod -g 0 root

title: Ensure accounts in /etc/passwd use shadowed passwords
description: Local accounts can use shadowed passwords. With shadowed passwords, the passwords are saved in shadow password file, /etc/shadow, encrypted by a salted one-way hash. Accounts with a shadowed password have an x in the second field in /etc/passwd. Audit: Passes when every account in /etc/passwd has x in the password field.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.1 Ensure accounts in /etc/passwd use shadowed passwords

audit.command: awk -F: '($2 != "x"){f=1} END{exit f}' /etc/passwd && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following command to set accounts to use shadowed passwords and migrate passwords in /etc/passwd to /etc/shadow: # pwconv Investigate to determine if the account is logged in and what it is being used for, to determine if it needs to be forced off.

title: Ensure /etc/shadow password fields are not empty
description: An account with an empty password field means that anybody may log in as that user without providing a password. Audit: Passes when no account in /etc/shadow has an empty password field (needs root).
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 7.2.2 Ensure /etc/shadow password fields are not empty

audit.command: [ -r /etc/shadow ] || exit 1; awk -F: '($2 == ""){f=1} END{exit f}' /etc/shadow && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: If any accounts in the /etc/shadow file do not have a password, run the following command to lock the account until it can be determined why it does not have a password: # passwd -l <username> Also, check to see if the account is logged in and investigate what it is being used for to determine if it needs to be forced off.

title: Ensure cramfs kernel module is not available
description: The cramfs filesystem type is a compressed read-only Linux filesystem embedded in small footprint systems. A cramfs image can be used without having to first decompress the image.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1.1 Ensure cramfs kernel module is not available

audit.command: m=cramfs; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/cramfs*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

remediation.guidance: Run the following to unload and disable the cramfs kernel module. Run the following commands to unload the cramfs kernel module: # modprobe -r cramfs 2>/dev/null # rmmod cramfs 2>/dev/null Perform the following to disable the cramfs kernel module: Create a file ending in .conf with install cramfs /bin/false in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: printf '%s\n' "" "install cramfs /bin/false" >> /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf Create a file ending in .conf with blacklist cramfs in the /etc/modprobe.d/ directory. Example: printf '%s\n' "" "blacklist cramfs" >> /etc/modprobe.d/cramfs.conf

title: Ensure freevxfs kernel module is not available
description: The freevxfs filesystem type is a free version of the Veritas type filesystem. This is the primary filesystem type for HP-UX operating systems.
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1.1.2 Ensure freevxfs kernel module is not available

audit.command: m=freevxfs; found=$(find /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel -path "*/freevxfs*" 2>/dev/null | head -n1); if [ -z "$found" ]; then echo compliant; exit 0; fi; lsmod | awk '{print $1}' | grep -Fxq -- "${m//-/_}" && { echo "$m is loaded"; exit 0; }; cfg=$(modprobe --showconfig 2>/dev/null); printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*blacklist\h+${m//-/_}\b" || { echo "$m is not blacklisted"; exit 0; }; printf '%s\n' "$cfg" | grep -Pq -- "^\h*install\h+${m//-/_}\h+(/usr)?/bin/(true|false)\b" || { echo "$m install is not disabled"; exit 0; }; echo compliant

title: Ensure default user umask is 027 or more restrictive
description: The user file-creation mode mask (umask) is use to determine the file permission for newly created directories and files. In Linux, the default permissions for any newly created directory is 0777 (rwxrwxrwx), and for any newly created file it is 0666 (rw- rw-rw-). Bits set in the umask are cleared in the resulting file mode. umask can be set with either octal or Symbolic values: • Octal (Numeric) Value - Represented by either three or four digits. ie umask 0027 or umask 027. If a four digit umask is used, the first digit is ignored. ... title: Ensure sshd DisableForwarding is enabled
description: The DisableForwarding parameter disables all forwarding features, including X11, ssh-agent(1), TCP and StreamLocal. This option overrides all other forwarding-related options and may simplify restricted configurations. • X11Forwarding provides the ability to tunnel X11 traffic through the connection to enable remote graphic connections. • ssh-agent is a program to hold private keys used for public key authentication. Through use of environment variables the agent can be located and automatically used for authentication when logging in to other machines using ssh. • SSH port forwarding is a mechanism in SSH for tunneling application ports from the client to the server, or servers to clients. ...
reference: CIS Azure Container Linux Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.10 Ensure sshd DisableForwarding is enabled

audit.command: alt0() { command -v grep >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: grep not installed"; return 1; }; command -v sshd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "step1: sshd not installed"; return 1; }; o=$(bash -c 'sshd -T | grep -i disableforwarding' 2>&1); printf '%s\n' "$o" | tr -s ' \t' '  ' | sed 's/^ //;s/ $//' | grep -Fxq -- 'disableforwarding yes' || { echo step1: missing 'disableforwarding yes'; return 1; }; }; if alt0; then echo compliant; fi
